doe_morris — MULTIVAR sensitivity op

• Datenarten: keine → design (ein Operator, der allein durch seine Argumente bestimmt ist — er nimmt kein Bild und keine Daten entgegen)

• Aufruf: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.doe_morris(r=10, factors=4, levels=4, seed=0, n_candidates=0) -> 'dict' (die Implementierung direkt: import sensitivity; sensitivity.doe_morris(r=10, factors=4, levels=4, seed=0, n_candidates=0) -> 'dict'; aus dem Register: opsmultivar.get("doe_morris"))

Verwendung

Morris-One-at-a-time-Screeningplan: r Trajektorien zu je k+1 Läufen -> design.

> Die ausführliche Beschreibung unten ist der Originaltext — Zusammenfassung und Überschriften sind übersetzt.

Each trajectory starts at a random point of the levels-level grid on the unit cube and moves one factor at a time by delta = levels / (2 (levels - 1)) (Morris 1991; with an even levels every grid level is equally likely to be visited), so r (k+1) runs give r elementary effects per factor. n_candidates > r draws that many trajectories and keeps r of them that are spread out: the trajectory distance of Campolongo et al. 2007 (sum over point pairs of their Euclidean distances), chosen greedily — a pair of the farthest trajectories first, then repeatedly the trajectory that adds the most distance (an approximation of their exhaustive search, stated in meta['selection']).

The coded matrix is 2u - 1 of the unit-cube points; meta keeps the trajectory bookkeeping that sens_morris needs (changed factor and sign per step).
